 A jinx? published at 12:31 GMT 12:31 GMT 
 Norwich 0-0 Cardiff 
 Dafydd Pritchard 
BBC Sport Wales 
 Nice to see my esteemed colleague Simon (12:21 GMT) has jinxed this Norwich-Cardiff fixture with his (entirely justifiable) expectation of goals galore.
 I covered Cardiff's 3-3 draw with West Ham and 5-4 win over Burnley, and they were even more chaotic than the scores suggest.
 Norwich know they'll get chances today and, having scored at least three goals in each of their four successive wins, the Canaries have shown they can be clinical.
 On top of that, Cardiff have just two points on the road this season. Only Watford and Preston have fared worse.

 Jensen and De Norre return for Lions, QPR make four changes published at 12:25 GMT 12:25 GMT 
 Millwall v QPR (12:30 GMT) 
 Image source, Opta Goalkeeper Lukas Jensen and midfielder Casper de Norre are back in the Millwall side after lengthy injury absence, with Alex Neil making three further changes to the side that lost 3-0 at West Brom.
 Striker Lyndon Dykes starts against his former club, with Tairyk Arconte and Mark Sykes also coming into the line-up for the Lions.
 Max Crocombe, Jordi Osei-Tutu, Derek Mazou-Sacko, Luke Cundle and Josh Coburn are the men to make way.
 Image source, Opta QPR captain Jimmy Dunne is out of the matchday squad through injury, but Ilias Chair starts for the first time since early September and midfielder Nico Madsen is also back after a five-week absence.
 Dennis Cirkin and Jake Clarke-Salter also come into the Rangers starting XI, with Harvey Vale, Kwame Poku and Jonathan Varane dropping to the bench.

 Faltering Lions look for capital gains in Hoops clash published at 12:23 GMT 12:23 GMT 
 Millwall v QPR (12:30 GMT) 
 Image source, Shutterstock A lunchtime London derby might be just what Millwall
need to kick-start their stuttering campaign, having gone into the
international break on the back of successive 3-0 defeats at Birmingham and
West Brom.
 The Lions are undefeated in the past seven league
meetings with any of their neighbours from the capital, stretching back almost
three years to a 2-0 defeat at the hands of today’s opponents QPR.
 Having gone close to promotion last season, more was
expected of Alex Neil’s side but they resume their schedule 15th in the table,
six points short of the final play-off spot – which is currently occupied by
the Hoops.
 “In the last two seasons since I’ve been here, we’ve
been very good in the second half of the year, so I’m hoping that’s a trend
that’s going to continue,” the Millwall boss told BBC Radio London .
 Like their hosts, Rangers have suffered heavy defeats
in their past two games on the road – at Birmingham and Southampton – but their
recent run also included big victories against Derby and promotion-chasing
Swansea.
 The two sides have already met once at the start of
the season, with Millwall triumphing in a low-scoring penalty shootout after a
1-1 draw in the first round of the League Cup.

 Goals galore at Carrow Road? published at 12:21 GMT 12:21 GMT 
 Norwich v Cardiff (12:30 GMT) 
 Simon Davies 
BBC Radio Wales commentator 
 Image source, Huw Evans Picture Agency If recent form is anything to go by, do not take your eyes off events at Carrow Road.
 Hosts Norwich City are in blistering form, winning their past four matches while scoring 15 goals in the process. 
 That run includes a 3-1 win at Charlton, a 3-2 home thriller against Watford, a 4-0 rout of Derby, and a 5-0 demolition of Bristol City last time out.
 Cardiff City, meanwhile, have been involved in pure chaos. 
 The Bluebirds arrive in Norfolk on the back of a 3-3 draw with West Ham and a nine-goal thriller of a 5-4 victory over Burnley after being 4-1 down.
 So don’t expect a goalless draw today… famous last words!

 One change for Norwich, three for Cardiff published at 12:19 GMT 12:19 GMT 
 Norwich v Cardiff (12:30 GMT) 
 Image source, Opta Norwich City boss Philippe Clement makes just one change from the side that thrashed Bristol City at Ashton Gate before the international break.
 Kenny McLean comes back into the midfield in place of Sam Field, who drops to the bench.
 Image source, Opta Brian Barry-Murphy makes three changes for Cardiff City from their blockbuster 5-4 comeback win over Burnley last timeout.
 Yousef Salech earns himself a start after bagging to goals against the Clarets, while Calum Scanlon and Ronan Kpakio also come into the side.
 Cian Ashford is among the subs but Joel Bagan misses out through suspension and Perry Ng is not the squad.
 4 1 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Canaries and Bluebirds flying high together? published at 12:17 GMT 12:17 GMT 
 Norwich v Cardiff (12:30 GMT) 
 Image source, Shutterstock We might be in for a humdinger at Carrow Road this afternoon with the way these two were going before the international break.
 There have been 18 goals scored in the past four games involving Norwich City and 29 in Cardiff City's previous six - we make that 47 goals in 10 games when one of them is playing.
 Bonkers.
 Both have also been gaining altitude in the Championship table, with the Canaries bouncing back from five straight defeats to pick up 12 points from a possible 12 to rise nine places from 21st to 12th, just three points behind the play-off places.
 As for the Bluebirds, three of their four wins this season have come in their past six matches (D2 L1), which has helped them pull away from the relegation zone to 14th - and they are now closer to the top eight than the bottom three.

 Larin returns for Saints; One change for Rams published at 12:15 GMT 12:15 GMT 
 Southampton v Derby (12:30 GMT) 
 Image source, Opta Southampton striker Cyle Larin returns after five weeks out but full-back James Bree and forward Leo Scienza both miss out with injuries.
 Bree's absence means one of midfield duo Flynn Downes or James Ward-Prowse is likely to fill in at right-back.
 Image source, Opta Derby make just the one change from the side that started the 3-1 win against Bolton last time out.
 Alex Mowatt comes in for Lewis Travis in midfield as the Rams look to secure back-to-back league wins for the first time since March.

 Saints without Bree and Scienza for Derby game published at 12:12 GMT 12:12 GMT 
 Southampton v Derby (12:30 GMT) 
 Dan George 
BBC Sport at St Mary's Stadium 
 Image source, BBC Sport Hello and a very good afternoon from a sunny St Mary's Stadium. 
 Championship football is back, and Southampton are playing for the first time since head coach Tonda Eckert was handed a new contract on Friday. 
 They host a struggling Derby County side this afternoon, but face a few challenges of their own going into the game with some key players out. 
 Saints are without Leo Scienza and James Bree today, despite the latter being the face of today's matchday programme. 
 The Rams will be hoping that they can build on their win against Bolton before the the international break, as they look to climb out of the relegation zone.
 4 1 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Can Rams shock Saints? published at 12:10 GMT 12:10 GMT 
 Southampton v Derby (12:30 GMT) 
 Image source, Getty Images Southampton's storming form was brought to a surprise end before the international break when they lost 1-0 at lowly Preston.
 They'll be looking to get back on track today against a struggling Derby side who brought an end to their own dreadful run of form with a 3-1 win over Bolton two weeks ago.
 Travelling Rams fans, who have not seen their men win here since February 2007, will no doubt be aware of the Saints' ominous home form. They're unbeaten in 17 in front of their own fans.
